items.title: Vulnerabilities in nginx Affecting Cisco Products: November 2026
items.one_liner: Update your nginx deployments to versions 1.31.9 or 1.30.7 to patch five critical remote code execution vulnerabilities.
items.summary: On November 18, 2026, nginx released updates fixing multiple critical remote code execution vulnerabilities affecting releases 1.9.5 through 1.31.8. The issues are resolved in mainline release 1.31.9 and stable release 1.30.7. Five specific CVEs were assigned covering flaws in the mail proxy, HTTP/2, HTTP/3, and resolver modules. Administrators are advised to update to the patched releases immediately.
items.bottom_line: Unpatched nginx servers between versions 1.9.5 and 1.31.8 face critical remote code execution risks across multiple modules.

items.title: CVE-2026-123633 Portfolio Status: Impact of NGINX Vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123007) on Palo Alto Networks Products (Severity: CRITICAL)
items.one_liner: Palo Alto Networks products running specific PAN-OS versions with HTTP/2 enabled are vulnerable to critical NGINX RCE flaws.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks assessed the impact of two critical NGINX vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, affecting its PAN-OS and Panorama products. CVE-2026-123633 is a use-after-free issue in HTTP/2 proxy handling, while CVE-2026-123007 is an integer underflow leading to a heap-based buffer overflow. Both flaws allow unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or crash worker processes if HTTP/2 is enabled. Customers can mitigate the exposure by disabling HTTP/2 on PAN-OS and Panorama.
items.bottom_line: Disabling HTTP/2 on PAN-OS and Panorama provides an immediate workaround against critical NGINX RCE flaws.

items.title: China attackers deployed AI agents that autonomously found and exploited a 0-day to take over a university server
items.one_liner: The first confirmed use of autonomous AI agents to successfully exploit a zero-day vulnerability marks a significant escalation in the threat landscape.
items.summary: Suspected Chinese state-linked attackers have successfully deployed autonomous AI agents to identify and exploit a zero-day vulnerability in a university server. The agents used the open-source penetration-testing framework 'Cairn' to map API endpoints and exploit a path traversal flaw in the MONAI Label medical imaging application. Before this success, the agents autonomously attempted various failed attacks, including credential spraying and exploiting Redis and Log4Shell vulnerabilities, over a 48-hour period. This incident highlights the growing capability of AI agents to conduct multi-stage, adaptive cyberattacks without human intervention.
items.bottom_line: The deployment of autonomous AI agents for zero-day exploitation demonstrates that attackers can now conduct adaptive, multi-stage intrusions at machine speed.

items.title: Microsoft's official Python agent framework hijacked to distribute malware
items.one_liner: Microsoft's official PyPI account was compromised to push malicious agent-framework updates that actively harvest cloud and developer credentials.
items.summary: Microsoft's official Python agent-framework package on PyPI was hijacked to distribute info-stealing malware via versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2. The malicious versions actively request and exfiltrate fresh identity tokens for GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, and Azure to an external webhook without ever needing to be explicitly imported by the developer. The compromise points to unauthorized access to an administrator account within Microsoft's GitHub organization. As a result, developers utilizing these versions must immediately inspect their environments and revoke exposed credentials.
items.bottom_line: Official packages from major publishers can be backdoored via compromised administrator credentials, turning trusted dependencies into credential harvesters.

items.title: ZDI-26-1033: (0Day) (Pwn2Own) United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP GetConfiguration Stack-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.one_liner: An unauthenticated RCE zero-day in Grizzl-E Smart EV chargers allows network-adjacent code execution via OCPP.
items.summary: A stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability exists in United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers within the handling of OCPP GetConfiguration requests, allowing unauthenticated network-adjacent attackers to achieve remote code execution. ZDI made multiple unsuccessful attempts to contact the vendor regarding the vulnerability discovered during Pwn2Own Automotive 2026. The only salient mitigation strategy is to restrict network interaction with the vulnerable device. A coordinated public release of the advisory occurred on November 18, 2026.

items.title: Jenkins Security Advisory 2026-10-28
items.one_liner: Jenkins security updates patch a critical XStream remote code execution flaw and several privilege escalation vulnerabilities.
items.summary: Jenkins released a security advisory addressing multiple critical vulnerabilities across its deliverables. A deserialization flaw in XStream configuration handling in Jenkins 2.587 and earlier (LTS 2.580.1 and earlier) fails to apply the deserialization filter to classes referenced by the resolves-to attribute, enabling remote code execution for authenticated users with config posting permissions. Other fixed issues include a stored cross-site scripting flaw via unconstrained collection elements, arbitrary code execution in the controller JVM via unverified agent launch command conversions, and arbitrary file reading by following symbolic links during item renaming.
items.bottom_line: Update Jenkins to version 2.588 or LTS 2.580.2 immediately to fix critical deserialization RCE, XSS, and arbitrary file read vulnerabilities.

claims.support_span: For backward compatibility with older agent configurations, Jenkins 2.587 and earlier, LTS 2.580.1 and earlier converts the launch commands they contain into launchers provided by this plugin. This conversion does not check whether the launch command has been approved by an administrator, allowing attackers with Agent/Configure permission to execute arbitrary code in the context of the Jenkins controller JVM.

items.title: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938): Find affected Java in your container images
items.one_liner: A new RCE in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder requires immediate attention if you are running Java on x86-64 hardware with AVX-512 VBMI.
items.summary: A critical remote code execution vulnerability, dubbed 'Java4Shell' (CVE-2026-114938), has been identified in the OpenJDK Base64 decoder. The flaw affects systems running on x86-64 processors with AVX-512 VBMI instructions, allowing unauthenticated attackers to trigger memory corruption. Oracle has released patches in its November 2026 security update, and container scanning tools are being updated to detect vulnerable Java runtimes within images. ARM-based processors, such as AWS Graviton, are not impacted by this specific vulnerability.
items.bottom_line: If your infrastructure runs on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI, you are at risk of unauthenticated RCE via Java4Shell and must patch your JDK immediately.

items.title: Hackers Exploit Cisco Expressway Flaw CVE-2026-76466 to Breach Russian Organization
items.one_liner: Attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-76466, a critical root-level RCE in Cisco Expressway, for lateral network movement.
items.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical remote code execution vulnerability, CVE-2026-76466 with a CVSS score of 9.8, in Cisco Expressway Series devices to breach networks. The vulnerability stems from persistent cookies and weak client certificate checks, allowing unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary OS commands as root. In the first confirmed attack in the wild, intruders compromised internet-facing Expressway boxes at a Russian organization, pivoted to internal cluster nodes, and staged custom Python scripts for lateral movement. Security firm F6 identified specific indicators of compromise, including Erlang system log entries showing nodeup connections from 'wombat@127.0.0.1'.

Affected product: Cisco Expressway Series X15.5.3
items.bottom_line: Unpatched Cisco Expressway devices exposed to the internet are actively targeted for root-level compromises and internal network pivoting.

items.title: Cisco Informational for Emergency Distrust of eMudhra Root and Intermediate Certificate Authorities
items.one_liner: Private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates are critically broken, allowing instant brute-force acquisition and triggering emergency distrust.
items.summary: Between October 17 and October 20, 2026, Cisco issued an informational advisory regarding a critical security compromise involving eMudhra-managed Certificate Authorities. A security researcher demonstrated that the private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were fundamentally broken due to an error in their Key Generation Ceremony in April 2025. This flaw allows malicious actors to brute-force acquire the private keys within seconds, prompting emergency distrust measures. Cisco's review indicates that products not explicitly listed in their advisory remain unaffected.
items.bottom_line: Compromised eMudhra intermediate certificate authority private keys can be brute-forced instantly, requiring immediate emergency distrust across systems.

items.title: Autonomy Logic OpenPLC Runtime
items.one_liner: A critical authentication bypass in OpenPLC Runtime allows unauthenticated attackers to create admin accounts, threatening industrial control systems.
items.summary: CISA has issued an advisory for Autonomy Logic OpenPLC Runtime versions 4.2.4 and earlier due to a vulnerability (CVE-2026-126088) that allows unauthenticated users to create admin accounts. The flaw affects critical infrastructure sectors including energy, water, and manufacturing. Users are urged to isolate control system networks from the internet and business networks, and to utilize secure remote access methods like VPNs. No public exploitation has been reported, but the potential for unauthorized administrative access poses a significant risk to industrial control systems.
items.bottom_line: Operators of OpenPLC Runtime must immediately isolate their control systems from the internet to prevent unauthorized administrative access.

items.one_liner: Update GitHub Enterprise Server to patch a stored XSS vulnerability that could lead to unauthorized SSH key injection.
items.summary: A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in GitHub Enterprise Server allowed organization members with custom-property management permissions to inject malicious code. By storing HTML in a single-select custom-property option, an attacker could force another member to execute actions, potentially adding an attacker-controlled SSH key to the victim's account. Exploitation required specific conditions, including a second manager attempting to remove the poisoned option during a sudo session.
items.bottom_line: GitHub Enterprise Server versions prior to 3.23 were vulnerable to an XSS attack that could allow unauthorized SSH key addition to victim accounts.

items.title: We caught the agent-framework PyPI compromise six minutes after it published
items.one_liner: Compromised versions of the Microsoft agent-framework package on PyPI silently exfiltrate credentials on every Python startup.
items.summary: Microsoft's agent-framework meta-package on PyPI was compromised in versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, deploying a credential-stealing startup hook that ran every time Python started. The malicious .pth hook triggered a telemetry script that collected environment variables, token caches, and cloud endpoints from running processes, exfiltrating them via a Base64-encoded and zlib-compressed POST request to an external webhook. Elastic Security Labs flagged the package six minutes after publication, and PyPI removed both versions within an hour. Anyone who used those versions on a host should assume all secrets on that host are compromised and pin back to version 1.26.0.
items.bottom_line: Immediately revoke all secrets and pin back to version 1.26.0 if your systems ever downloaded agent-framework versions 1.26.1 or 1.26.2.

claims.text: The compromised package is the meta-package, a thin wrapper used to pull in the different framework dependencies.
claims.support_span: The compromised package is the meta-package, a thin wrapper used to pull in the different framework dependencies.

claims.text: Both versions shipped a .pth startup hook... so the credential stealer ran every time Python started on the host.

items.one_liner: Optimize large agent tool inventories in Gemini apps using server-side Tool Retrieval to lower token overhead and latency.
items.summary: Google has announced Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API, designed to reduce token bloat and latency when agentic applications connect to dozens or hundreds of functions. items.summary: A critical unauthenticated deserialization vulnerability in Apache Roller's XML-RPC endpoint, tracked as CVE-2026-129448 with a CVSS score of 9.8, is under active exploitation in the wild. items.title: 10-Year-Old NGINX HTTP/2 Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code on Servers
items.one_liner: A critical decade-old unauthenticated RCE flaw in NGINX HTTP/2 allows attackers to run code as worker processes and potentially gain host root access, requiring an immediate upgrade to version 1.31.9 or 1.30.7.
items.summary: A decade-old critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-123007, dubbed 'nginx2root,' has been discovered in NGINX's HTTP/2 support, allowing unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on vulnerable servers. The flaw impacts NGINX open-source versions 1.9.5 through 1.31.8 and various NGINX Plus releases, where successful exploitation grants code execution with NGINX worker process privileges. Security researchers demonstrated that bypassing ASLR is possible, and attackers can further escalate to root privileges on host machines by chaining this vulnerability with separate kernel bugs like SCTP issues, even within Docker containers. Vendor F5 has released patched versions 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 alongside fixes for four additional code execution vulnerabilities, prompting administrators to upgrade immediately and perform a full restart to replace running binaries.

Fixed Versions: NGINX Open Source 1.31.9 and 1.30.7
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated attackers can achieve remote code execution on any server running unpatched NGINX with HTTP/2 enabled by exploiting CVE-2026-123007.

items.one_liner: Git 2.56.1 and backports fix six critical security flaws, including code execution during cloning and path traversal.
items.summary: The Git project has released security patches across multiple maintenance series, culminating in Git 2.56.1, to address six vulnerabilities including arbitrary code execution, path traversal, and stack corruption. CVE-2026-111760 involves an integer truncation vulnerability during index handling that permits an attacker-controlled Git server to overwrite repository metadata or execute code during cloning. Other fixed issues include path traversal via protocol v2 HEAD advertisements (CVE-2026-113408), stack corruption from excessive GPG signatures during merges (CVE-2026-114467), and out-of-bounds reads when applying compressed binary patches. Administrators and developers should update Git installations and dependent applications immediately.

items.summary: The Nexter Blocks Pro WordPress plugin (versions 5.0.10 and below) contains a critical privilege escalation vulnerability (CVE-2026-125294). Because the required nonce is publicly available, the exploit chain is trivial to execute on default installations.

items.one_liner: Multi-tenant cloud operators running AMD hosts with nested virtualization must patch KVM immediately to prevent guest VMs from reading and writing host memory.
items.summary: A vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-99312 in Linux KVM allows guest virtual machines to access host memory on AMD hosts with nested virtualization enabled. items.summary: A newly disclosed unpatched Windows zero-day technique called FastUnlock allows individuals with physical access to a locked Windows PC to run programs without signing in, granting access to a limited user account (WSIAccount) rather than administrator privileges. Discovered by researchers using the handles MSNightmare and Nightmare Eclipse, the technique utilizes Windows' built-in Narrator screen reader to navigate the lock screen via a reachable Microsoft account through recovery options. Because many systems use BitLocker with TPM chips to automatically unlock drives at startup, the file system is already readable when the lock screen appears, meaning FastUnlock does not break disk encryption. Microsoft has not yet issued a fix, so users are advised to secure physical access, use startup PINs for BitLocker, and hibernate devices when unattended.
items.bottom_line: Physical access combined with an accessible Microsoft account allows unauthenticated users to execute programs on locked Windows machines via the FastUnlock zero-day.

Previously, KVM failed to force an MMU reset if paging was already disabled during an INIT event while L2 guest mode was active, leading to running L1 with a stale MMU context. The fix ensures that nested SVM environments properly handle INIT events regardless of prior paging status. The vulnerability carries a CVSS base score of 8.8.
key_facts: Affected component: Linux kernel KVM x86 subsystem
items.bottom_line: Apply Linux kernel patches addressing KVM MMU context stales during guest INIT emulation to secure nested virtualization environments.

items.title: Hackers Exploiting Critical Puppet RCE Flaw Affecting Enterprise Management Servers
items.one_liner: A critical deserialization flaw in Perforce Puppet Enterprise (CVE-2026-115731) is actively exploited in the wild, enabling full network takeover.
items.summary: CISA added a critical remote code execution vulnerability in Perforce Puppet Enterprise and Core to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following reports of active exploitation. Tracked as CVE-2026-115731 with a CVSS score of 9.4, the flaw stems from insecure deserialization in report-processing code that allows unauthenticated network attackers to execute arbitrary code as the service user. The bug was discovered with artificial intelligence assistance by Neodyme AG security researcher Alain Rödel, alongside a companion certificate authorization bypass CVE-2026-115732. Successful exploitation permits attackers to grab CA signing keys, impersonate hosts, deploy ransomware, and execute lateral movement across corporate networks. Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies have been instructed to apply patches under BOD 26-04 by December 1, 2026.
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated attackers can achieve remote code execution on Puppet servers via CVE-2026-115731 to harvest CA keys and compromise entire corporate fleets.

items.one_liner: Immediately patch the critical Java4Shell Base64 memory-corruption vulnerability affecting multiple enterprise Java applications.
items.summary: Oracle disclosed a critical 9.2-rated memory-corruption vulnerability in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder, dubbed 'Java4Shell' (CVE-2026-114938), which allows unauthenticated remote code execution or Java virtual machine crashes. Discovered by Calif.io, the vulnerability affects applications like Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, Apache Kafka, and Elasticsearch running on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI support enabled. CISA and security vendors have urged immediate patching of affected Java versions.
items.bottom_line: A critical memory-corruption flaw in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder allows unauthenticated remote code execution across popular Java applications.

claims.text: The United States Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency has urged Java users to immediately patch a high-severity flaw in the software, which attackers can use to crash the Java virtual machine or achieve unauthenticated remote code execution.
claims.support_span: The United States Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has urged Java users to immediately patch a high-severity flaw in the software, which attackers can use to crash the Java virtual machine or achieve unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE).

claims.text: Calif.io tested the flaw, which it named Java4Shell, and found applications including Keycloak, Atlassian's Jira and Confluence, Jenkins, Apache Kafka Broker, and Elasticsearch are susceptible to RCE.
claims.support_span: Calif, which also helped to find the PHP2Shell flaw, says the flaw is a memory-corruption vulnerability in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder. “Base64 is a very common way of representing binary data as text. It is used in authentication protocols, to encode file uploads, and to deliver network messages,” the company explained. “To decode Base64 faster, OpenJDK uses specialized x86-64 CPU instructions to process many bytes at once.” “We discovered a bug in that optimized machine-level code that lets malformed input overwrite neighboring memory. With careful exploitation, the corruption can reveal sensitive memory, as Heartbleed did, or lead to remote code execution. The corruption itself can be triggered by just 64 A characters followed by a single =:” Calif applied the CVSS 4.0 bug-rating scheme and gave the flaw a critical-rated score of 9.2/10.

items.one_liner: An unvalidated metadata path traversal flaw in ansible-core allows malicious collections to delete directories and write arbitrary files.
items.summary: A path traversal vulnerability exists in ansible-core during the collection installation process via ansible-galaxy collection install. Because namespace and name fields inside collection artifact metadata are unvalidated for path containment, a malicious collection artifact delivered via local files, URLs, source directories, git repositories, or dependencies can redirect the destination outside the configured path. This causes ansible-galaxy to delete an existing user-writable directory and overwrite it with attacker-controlled files. The vulnerability carries a CVSS base score of 8.1.
items.bottom_line: Avoid installing untrusted Ansible collections until ansible-core is patched against metadata-driven path traversal.

items.title: Suspected Chinese APT Rebuilds EggStreme Malware After Exposure
items.one_liner: Suspected Chinese APT actors re-engineered the EggStreme malware framework within days of public exposure by Bitdefender.
items.summary: A suspected Chinese advanced persistent threat (APT) group rapidly rebuilt components of its EggStreme fileless malware framework after security firm Bitdefender publicly exposed it in September 2025. Targeting military and government organizations in the Philippines and Taiwan, the operators modified configuration protection mechanisms within 12 days of the report, deployed new ciphers, and updated loaders. The EggStremeAgent backdoor also dropped its raw TCP connections in favor of mutual TLS, integrated Windows domain mapping, and added in-memory PowerShell execution while stripping out keyloggers. Although the infrastructure shifted toward campaign-specific servers, defenders can still track the framework through constant behaviors such as DLL sideloading, file share movement, in-memory execution, and mutual TLS.

items.title: GnuPG Warns Critical GPGME Flaw Could Expose App Data via Malicious OpenPGP Keys
items.summary: A malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID can trigger a critical memory bug in GPGME, the standard library that programs use to work with GnuPG. The GnuPG project warned yesterday that the flaw could be used to steal data from affected applications and has released fixed versions. items.title: The forced audit: how AuditTeam’s OpsAgent framework masks ransomware as consulting

items.summary: An active threat group known as AuditTeam has been deploying a modular framework called OpsAgent to compromise organizations across seven countries between January and October 2026. After encrypting corporate systems, AuditTeam drops ransom notes demanding an 'Audit & Consulting fee' in exchange for vulnerability reports rather than data leakage. items.title: External sandboxes for coding agents
items.one_liner: A new external sandboxing pattern isolates code executed by local AI coding agents using WebAssembly, Apple Containers, or QEMU.
items.summary: Simon Willison and AI research lab Prime Radiant have introduced the external sandbox pattern to isolate code executed by AI coding agents from the host machine. To demonstrate the pattern, they released three open-source sandbox server implementations providing a unified localhost API: external-sandbox-v86 using Node.js with v86 and Alpine Linux in WebAssembly, external-sandbox-container using Apple Containers, and external-sandbox-quicksand utilizing Microsoft's Quicksand library bundling QEMU and Alpine Linux. These sandbox servers can be integrated with coding assistants like Claude Code, Codex, or Pi, and include optional HTTP/HTTPS allow-list proxies and credential replacement mechanisms for secure API calls.
items.bottom_line: You can now run local AI coding agents inside isolated WebAssembly or containerized sandboxes to prevent prompt injection attacks from damaging your host machine.

items.summary: JFrog Security outlines how the traditional vulnerability remediation playbook has broken down in the AI era due to frontier models discovering zero-days and generating working exploits before disclosures or patches exist. items.title: How I Found a $113,337 AF_ALG Linux Local Privilege Escalation Before Copy Fail
items.one_liner: A retrospective look at uncovering a $113,337 Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw in the AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem via unprivileged socket APIs.
items.summary: Security researcher Muhammad Alifa Ramdhan details the discovery of CVE-2025-39964, a critical race condition vulnerability in the Linux kernel's AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem that earned a $113,337 reward via Google's kernelCTF. Exploiting out-of-bounds access stemming from how AF_ALG handles inputs across unprivileged sockets, an ordinary user can escalate privileges to root or achieve container escape. Present in the kernel since 2011, this vulnerability preceded the widely known 'Copy Fail' flaw but highlights the same underlying kernel attack surface.
items.bottom_line: Unprivileged access to the Linux kernel's AF_ALG subsystem harbors deep race condition vulnerabilities capable of full privilege escalation and container escape.

items.title: The Growing Role of Digital Forensics in Criminal Investigations
items.one_liner: Digital forensics shapes 90% of criminal cases, requiring rigorous chain-of-custody protocols and expert verification to address tool limitations.
items.summary: Digital evidence now contributes to approximately 90 percent of criminal cases, transforming investigations across devices like smartphones, laptops, and cloud accounts. Standard forensic procedures require isolating seized devices from networks to prevent remote wiping, creating exact forensic images, and validating data integrity using cryptographic hash values with strict chain-of-custody logging. While forensic tools extract extensive logs, messages, and location records, analysts must account for limitations such as device encryption, cloud-only data storage, and potential inaccuracy in cell tower positioning. Defense strategies routinely rely on third-party experts to verify hash values, timezone settings, and the reliability of automated tool outputs.
key_facts: Contribution: ~90% of criminal cases involve digital evidence
items.bottom_line: Digital evidence is foundational to modern legal investigations, but its admissibility and reliability depend strictly on verifiable chain-of-custody and forensic hygiene.

items.title: The cryptography behind electronic voting (and why paper ballots are still essential)
items.summary: As millions of Americans vote in today’s U.S. midterms, most will use paper ballots, which are protected by strict chain-of-custody protocols and, in some cases, statistical audits. After all, cryptography and other security advancements have enabled secure electronic systems for many applications. In fact, cryptography can be used to provide two essential safeguards in elections: keeping (1) individual votes secret while (2) making the final tally independently verifiable.
